events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Alexander, NC; Catawba, NC
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Alexander County in the piedmont of North Carolina...
Catawba County in the piedmont of North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 230 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots. Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.  A
few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A
small culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 833 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicates that an axis of torrential
rainfall is pivoting across northwestern Catawba and Alexander
counties, capable of producing accumulations of 0.75-1.5 inches
in less than 30-45 minutes.  This rainfall is occurring on top of
saturated soils due to a prolonged period of light to moderate
showers that have occurred over the county since yesterday
morning. Widespread, storm-total rainfall of the 2.5-4 inches
fell yesterday. The current torrential rainfall will cause
swollen streams to rise further, potentially exceeding their
banks and flooding adjacent low-lying areas.  Poorly-draining
areas and roadways will likely seem some flooding develop over
the next 60-90 minutes as runoff works into drainages and onto
road surfaces.

High flows will also be working down Henry Fork, Jacob Fork, and
well as the mainstem Catawba River due to upstream heavy
rainfall.  These flows may impact low-lying areas including
parks, farmland, and woodland.

- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Hickory, Newton, Taylorsville, St. Stephens, Conover, Longview,
Bethlehem, Maiden, Hildebran and Stony Point.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Wasatch Plateau/Book Cliffs; Eastern Juab/Millard Counties; Central Mountains; Sanpete Valley; Sevier Valley; Castle Country; San Rafael Swell; Southwest Utah; Lower Washington County; Zion National Park; Southern Mountains; Upper Sevier River Valleys; Bryce Canyon Country; South Central Utah; Capitol Reef National Park and Vicinity; Western Canyonlands; Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, Central Mountains, Eastern Juab/Millard Counties, San
Rafael Swell, Sanpete Valley, Sevier Valley, Wasatch Plateau/Book
Cliffs, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef National Park and
Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell, South Central
Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper Sevier River Valleys, Western
Canyonlands, Lower Washington County, Southwest Utah and Zion
National Park. This also includes recent burn scars such as
Forsyth, Cottonwood, Silver King, France Canyon, and Monroe Canyon.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars. Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may
occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Anomalously high moisture from the remnants of Tropical Storm
Rachel will continue to impact the region. While this is expected
to be a long duration rainfall event, scattered instances of
heavier rainfall rates are expected with stronger storms yielding
flash flooding concerns given saturated soils and prior burn
scars.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Great Salt Lake Desert and Mountains; Tooele and Rush Valleys; Eastern Box Elder County; Northern Wasatch Front; Salt Lake Valley; Utah Valley; Cache Valley/Utah Portion; Wasatch Back; Bear Lake and Bear River Valley; Wasatch Mountains I-80 North; Wasatch Mountains South of I-80; Western Uinta Mountains; Western Uinta Basin; Western Millard and Juab Counties
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Western
Millard and Juab Counties, Bear Lake and Bear River Valley, Cache
Valley/Utah Portion, Eastern Box Elder County, Great Salt Lake
Desert and Mountains, Northern Wasatch Front, Salt Lake Valley,
Tooele and Rush Valleys, Utah Valley, Wasatch Back, Wasatch
Mountains I-80 North, Wasatch Mountains South of I-80, Western
Uinta Basin and Western Uinta Mountains. This includes recent burn
scars such as Rocky Canyon.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and recent burn scars. Flooding may occur in poor
drainage and urban areas. Extensive street flooding and flooding of
creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moisture associated with the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel
will continue to spread into northern Utah producing a prolonged
rainfall event. In particular, moisture interacting with a
frontal boundary across far northern Utah may yield locally
heavier rainfall totals compared to other locations. As a result,
areal flooding is possible across northern Utah.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Ashe, NC; Watauga, NC; Wilkes, NC
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Urban areas and small streams flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...South Central Ashe County in northwestern North Carolina...
Watauga County in northwestern North Carolina...
Southwestern Wilkes County in northwestern North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring. Several streams and rivers
continue to rise due to recent heavy rain, including the Watauga
River near the communities of Banner Elk and Foscoe, where multiple
side roads crossing the river may remain flooded through 11 AM.
These include Sleepy Hollow Lane, Clubhouse Drive, and Aldridge
Road. Near the Town of Boone, portions of Deerfield Road and Bamboo
Road are flooded and impassible. Other low-water crossings within
the warning area also remain inundated with water and may not be
passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 826 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
that heavy rain has exited the warning area. However, between 4.5
and 7.5 inches of rain have fallen since Saturday morning, and
runoff from heavy rain that fell since 6 AM continues to collect
in area creeks and streams.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Flat Branch, Dugger Creek, Left Prong Stony Fork, Grassy Creek,
Laurel Fork, Mill Creek, Meat Camp Creek, Elk Creek, Dutch Creek,
Norris Fork, Fall Creek, Brushy Fork and Little Dugger Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Boone, Blowing Rock, Deep Gap, Todd, Foscoe, Seven Devils and
Aho.
- For flooding safety information, please visit
http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
FFWVEF

The National Weather Service in Las Vegas has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Clark County in southern Nevada...

* Until 830 AM PDT.

* At 533 AM PDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.75 and 1.5 inches of
rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Las Vegas, North Las Vegas, Summerlin, Spring Valley, Lone
Mountain, The Strip, Centennial Hills, Mountains Edge, Fremont
Street, Blue Diamond, Enterprise, Red Rock Canyon, Paradise,
Aliante, Southern Highlands, Las Vegas Ballpark, Red Rock Canyon
Campground, North Las Vegas Airport, Allegiant Stadium and Harry
Reid International Airport.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued
a Flood Warning for the following rivers in South Carolina...North
Carolina...

(English) Broad River Near at Shelby Hwy (SC 18), 4 W Blacksburg
affecting Cherokee and Cleveland Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...(English) Broad River near at Shelby Hwy (SC 18), 4 W
Blacksburg.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 to 16.0 feet, Action Stage Flooding continues.
Areas of Buffalo Creek may flood due to backwater effects. The
Broad River may also be flooding River Rd. and Little Hope Rd. near
US 29.  Adjacent farmland and low-lying area flooding is
continuing.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:00 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 15.1 feet and rising.
- Bankfull stage is 13.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this afternoon to a crest of 16.7 feet this evening. It will then
fall below flood stage just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
